classifications.label: Systematic environmental coupling: a common physical driver (temperature, vibration, magnetic field, or air pressure) is anti-correlated with time, affecting all four instruments with instrument-specific lags (4–8 days).

Measurement protocol or operator dependence: lab and observatory streams are run by different people or times of day, introducing a systematic bias that manifests as anti-correlation when cross-checked.

Undetected calibration drift in one or more instruments, masked by baseline averaging: a slow drift in one instrument over days 1–10 creates apparent anti-correlation with others when baselines are compared.

Chance clustering in a small sample: with only n=18–36 for most cross-checks after offset alignment, negative correlations at specific lags could arise from random sampling, even though the choice of 'best' offset introduces selection bias.
